title: Fix composer menu keyboard scrolling
description: When navigating the @ mention and slash command menus with arrow keys, keep the selected item scrolled into view and handle wraparound cleanly so returning to the top also scrolls back to the top.

title: Add beads issue detection to project artifacts
description: Detect whether a project directory contains a .beads/ directory. If so, run 'bd list --json' to fetch open issues and include them in ProjectArtifacts. Add a BeadIssue type to types.ts and a beadsIssues field to ProjectArtifacts.

title: Investigate Claude SDK exit-listener accumulation on startup
description: Startup can emit MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 exit listeners added to [process]. Current evidence points to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk registering process.on("exit") inside its CLI/runtime path for each managed SDK session. This likely becomes visible once relay restores enough managed sessions at boot. Investigate whether we can reuse a single SDK runtime, defer session creation, explicitly close listeners, or work around/upstream the SDK behavior without masking real leaks.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Observed after the managed-session provider refactor. Local evidence: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/cli.js registers process.on("exit", ...) in its main path, and relay now creates one SDK-backed managed session per restored managed instance at startup.

title: Add REST endpoint for beads issues
description: Add GET /api/projects/:id/issues endpoint that runs 'bd list --json' in the project directory and returns the results. Consider caching since bd list requires spawning a process.

title: Codex session discovery — scan ~/.codex/sessions/
Support GitLab issues and merge requests

title: Support GitHub Issues in project issues view
description: The issues board currently only supports beads (bd) issues. Extend it to also display GitHub Issues for projects that have a linked GitHub repo (via ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths). Fetch open/closed GitHub issues via gh issue list --json, normalize into a unified ProjectIssue type, show alongside beads issues in the kanban board with a source badge/icon, and link back to the GitHub issue URL in the drawer.

title: Add Codex adapter
description: Add first-class Codex provider support for relay-managed sessions only. The rollout should preserve current Claude behavior while introducing provider-aware session creation, persistence, managed execution, and UI capability handling for Codex. This epic explicitly excludes Codex external-session discovery, transcript scanning from ~/.codex, and terminal/UI handoff parity with Claude.
acceptance_criteria: Codex can be used for managed sessions created and driven from the relay UI without regressing existing Claude flows; work is split into provider foundation, managed session adapter, managed-session persistence/history, UI capabilities, and docs/tests; Codex external session discovery is explicitly out of scope.

Saved transcripts live under  with an index in . First implementation should treat permission/sandbox behavior as provider-specific instead of trying to preserve Claude’s approval flow verbatim.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Local runtime probe summary: managed Codex work should target codex exec --json for first turns and codex exec resume --json for follow-up turns. The live JSON stream uses thread.started, turn.started, item.started/item.completed, and turn.completed events. Persisted session data is indexed in ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl and stored under ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/. Permission and sandbox UX should be treated as provider-specific because Codex does not expose Claude-style approval callbacks in exec mode.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Scope correction on 2026-03-08: Codex support is managed-session-only for this rollout. Do not implement Codex external session discovery, transcript import of terminal-created sessions, or Claude-style terminal/UI handoff behavior. Any persistence/replay work should apply only to relay-created Codex sessions.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Architecture reference for this epic: use pingdotgg/t3code as the design baseline for provider layering. In particular, borrow the split between provider/session contracts and canonical runtime events (packages/contracts/src/provider.ts and providerRuntime.ts), plus the isolated Codex runtime manager pattern (apps/server/src/codexAppServerManager.ts), rather than threading Codex conditionals through the whole codebase.

title: Make provider selection a first-class concept
description: Replace Claude-specific assumptions in core session creation and persistence with an explicit provider identity. Model this after t3code's separation between provider contracts and runtime orchestration: provider kind/config/session metadata should be explicit, provider-specific runtime details should sit behind a clean factory boundary, and the rest of the app should depend on normalized provider state instead of raw CLI quirks. This includes config/types for selecting a provider, provider-aware session metadata in the DB, and a clean factory boundary so InstanceManager does not hard-code Claude SDK vs Claude CLI selection.
acceptance_criteria: Instances can declare a provider kind; provider choice persists in SQLite; InstanceManager creates sessions through a provider-aware factory; existing Claude behavior remains default-compatible; no UI behavior changes required beyond plumbing.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Implemented provider as a first-class managed-session field across core types, create-instance payloads, and SQLite persistence. Managed restore now routes through provider-aware session creation instead of assuming the current default provider.

title: Add managed Codex session adapter
description: Implement a ProviderSession for relay-managed Codex sessions using the local codex CLI. Heavily reference t3code's Codex architecture: keep the Codex-specific process/event handling isolated in its own runtime manager/adapter, translate raw Codex JSON events into a canonical relay event shape, and avoid leaking Codex CLI details across InstanceManager and the UI. The adapter should support first-turn creation with codex exec --json, subsequent turns with codex exec resume --json, model overrides where supported, interruption/close semantics, and translation of Codex JSON events into relay output/activity/status messages. Scope is limited to sessions created and driven from the relay UI.
acceptance_criteria: A managed Codex instance created from the relay UI can be sent multiple turns; output streams into the existing UI; session IDs are captured and reused for resume; unsupported capabilities are surfaced cleanly instead of pretending Claude parity; tests cover the Codex event-stream mapping.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Implemented a managed Codex provider in src/core/providers/codex-cli.ts using codex exec --json and codex exec resume --json. InstanceManager now creates Codex sessions through the provider boundary, Codex thread IDs are captured into provider runtime bindings for subsequent resume, Codex event streams are mapped into relay output/activity/stats, and test/codex-cli.test.js covers the core event mapping. The new-session UI can now select Codex and hides/adapts Claude-only controls rather than pretending parity where Codex support is not there yet.

title: Support managed Codex session restore and history replay
description: Teach the relay to restore and replay Codex history for sessions that were created and managed by the relay itself. This includes persisting the provider/session metadata needed to resume managed Codex sessions after relay restarts and mapping saved Codex transcript events into relay history/state for those managed sessions only. External Codex session discovery and terminal-originated session import are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A relay-managed Codex session can survive relay restart with the right provider/session metadata; managed Codex history can be replayed into the UI as needed for restored sessions; no ~/.codex-wide discovery or import path is introduced.

title: Make the UI provider-aware for Codex capabilities
description: Update the server/UI contract so labels, controls, and warnings are provider-aware instead of Claude-branded. This includes managed instance creation/provider selection, message labeling, model/reasoning control visibility, permission/sandbox messaging, and any capability gating needed where Codex differs from Claude. Scope is limited to relay-managed Codex sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Users can choose Codex when creating a managed session; Claude-only controls or wording are hidden or adapted for Codex; provider-specific limitations are explicit in the UI; existing Claude UX stays intact.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Advanced the UI slice needed for managed Codex sessions: users can now choose Codex in the new-session form, Claude-only reasoning controls are hidden for Codex, permission/sandbox copy is provider-aware, and the form calls out the current Codex limitations. This issue stays open because it is still blocked on managed Codex restore/history parity work.

Document provider selection, managed-only Codex support, supported capabilities, and any intentionally missing parity in the first release. This task should not add documentation promising Codex external session discovery or terminal/UI handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Test coverage exists for provider selection and at least the core managed Codex adapter/restore paths; README and AGENTS.md describe the provider architecture and the managed-only Codex support boundary; docs stay aligned with any schema/config changes introduced by the implementation.

title: Introduce provider runtime bindings separate from Claude JSONL

Persist provider-owned runtime binding data alongside generic session metadata, modeled after t3code's ProviderSessionDirectory/ProviderSessionRuntime: provider kind, resume state, runtime payload, and runtime mode should be recoverable without scanning ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl. Claude JSONL parsing should remain a Claude-specific history/discovery mechanism, not the core managed-session source of truth. Acceptance: managed sessions can restore via persisted provider binding even if no Claude JSONL contract exists; InstanceManager no longer requires jsonlPath to persist managed sessions; Claude transcript watching remains supported as an optional/provider-specific path.

title: Investigate session discovery for Claude Code IDE plugins (VS Code, Cursor, Zed)
description: Research how Claude Code's IDE plugins (VS Code, Cursor, Zed) store their session data — JSONL paths, project directory encoding, process names, etc. Currently the relay discovers CLI sessions via ps + lsof and reads JSONL from ~/.claude/projects/. IDE plugins may use different paths, process names, or session formats. Investigate: where do IDE plugin sessions write JSONL? Do they use the same ~/.claude/projects/ directory structure? Are the process names different (e.g. not 'claude' in ps output)? What changes are needed in discoverExisting/scanAllSessions to pick up IDE sessions? Goal: surface IDE plugin sessions in the relay UI the same way we surface terminal CLI sessions.

title: Move managed approvals to request IDs instead of tool names
description: Replace the current approve_tool(toolName) flow with a provider-neutral request-response model inspired by t3code. Approval/user-input requests should carry stable request IDs plus provider-specific payload, and the manager/UI should answer them by request ID and decision rather than by bare tool name. This should preserve Claude support while making the API capable of Codex/Gemini-style command/file/user-input requests. Acceptance: provider contract exposes request IDs for pending approvals, transport/API carries requestId-based responses, manager routes approval responses without assuming tool-name identity, and Claude SDK permission flow still works through the new contract.
